text:
support_jen: Hey team, ACME reported a P99 jump from ~80ms to 480ms for embedding calls this morning. They say requests from EU clients are hitting US endpoints. Can we check routing/fallbacks? :frowning:
customer_acme: yes, we started seeing timeouts and higher latency around 07:12 UTC. Header shows x-client-region: eu-west-1 but backend shows us-east-1 in traces.
sre_oncall: grabbing traces now. do we have a trace id from the customer?
customer_acme: trace id: trace-8f3a9c; sample request at 07:13:05 UTC.
ome: I pulled the trace: shows an initial route to eu-west-1, then an immediate 302 to control-plane.us-east-1 and final egress from us-east-1. Looks like a fallback path triggered.
lee: interesting — could be an expired region cache on the edge causing a control-plane lookup that resolves to the wrong region. any config change overnight?
support_jen: no infra deploys listed, but deploy-bot logged a canary config push at 06:58 UTC: "canary: routing/fallback-policy=relaxed".
deploy-bot: canary routing/fallback-policy=relaxed deployed by ops-automation at 06:58 UTC.
sre_oncall: okay that matches. relaxed fallback allows cross-region fallback to maintain availability. But why choose us-east-1 for EU traffic? need to see routing table and client IP->region mapping for that customer.
ome: sending quick repro curl they can run to capture headers:

```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <redwood-key>" \ 
  -H "X-Client-Region: eu-west-1" \ 
  https://api.redwood.inference/v1/embeddings -d '{"input":"test"}'
```

in the response headers we want X-Served-Region and X-Fallback-Reason.
customer_acme: ran it, response headers: X-Served-Region: us-east-1, X-Fallback-Reason: region-unavailable-cache-miss, X-Trace: trace-8f3a9c.
lee: "region-unavailable-cache-miss" implies the edge didn't have a fresh mapping and hit control-plane; control-plane returned us-east-1 because of a stale preference attributed to ACME account (old onboarding default).
sre_oncall: confirm: account metadata shows preferred_region: eu-west-1 but last_updated: 2022-09-12. control-plane service that resolves region replicas had a bug in tie-breaker where missing health pings favored primary (us-east-1). we rolled a fix yesterday but only to primary; canary enabled relaxed fallback which made control-plane more willing to return any viable region. combined -> us-east-1 selection.
support_jen: proposed mitigation: 1) quickly set a customer-specific override to prefer eu-west-1 for ACME, 2) roll back canary for routing/fallback-policy, 3) patch control-plane tie-breaker.
ome: I applied account override -> set override_region=eu-west-1 for acme-corp. Should be effective within 30s.
sre_oncall: rolling back canary now. deploy-bot: rollback routing/fallback-policy canary executed at 07:42 UTC.
deploy-bot: routing/fallback-policy restored to conservative.
customer_acme: retested, P99 dropped back to ~85ms, X-Served-Region: eu-west-1. Thanks.
lee: follow-ups: add better trace annotation when control-plane returns non-preferred region (include reason code), add alert if >1% requests for an account served outside preferred region, and include account_region in cache key to avoid stale cross-account poisoning.
support_jen: opening a ticket for the control-plane bug and the trace/alert enhancements. tagging infra and product to review fallback policy default. :+1:
customer_acme: appreciate the quick turnaround. We'll keep monitoring and let you know if anything reappears.
